neighbours.label: the 'and' or comma right after a tidiness or purity adjective, where a second clean-state quality follows ('keep it neat and', 'purified and stable', 'clean, affordable'); the same coordination after other adjectives stays quiet
fire: Wipe the counters daily to keep them tidy and free of crumbs.
The lab buys only distilled and filtered water for its tests.
Guests praised the spotless, quiet rooms of the small hotel.
Brush the horse each morning to keep its coat neat and shiny.
The city wants safe, clean and reliable buses for everyone.
A refined and pure sample is needed to calibrate the device.
Rake the gravel paths so they stay tidy, even and weed-free.
The new filters supply fresh, sanitary water to the camp.
quiet: Wipe the counters daily because crumbs attract ants.
The lab buys only cheap and heavy glass for its tests.
Guests praised the friendly, quiet staff of the small hotel.
Brush the horse each morning before riding it to the field.
The city wants fast, frequent buses for everyone.
A rare and costly sample was lost during the move.
Rake the leaves into piles so the children can jump in them.
The new pumps supply warm, salty water to the pool.

predictions: ' and'/',' 0.4-1.1 after neat/purified/clean; after toxic/slow/cheap below 0.05
notes: Card: ' and'/',' after purified, neat, sunny, clean; the + pole promotes clean/clear. Probe: 'keep it neat and' 1.148, 'clean, affordable' 0.531, 'purified and stable' 0.498; 'toxic and volatile' 0.014, 'long, slow and boring' 0.005. 'keep it short' fired 0.600 at ' it' (a slot that predicts clean/neat), so no near miss uses 'keep it'. The code cache.clear() example scored 0.008 and is left out.
